conventions.commits: Conventional commits with DCO sign-off (inferred from CONTRIBUTING.md and REUSE.toml)
conventions.testing: Unit tests inline in language modules using tree-sitter Parser; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/; test pattern: parse_<lang>(src) helper, tree traversal with stack or cursor, query validation, capture extraction
conventions.linting: cargo clippy with deny-level rules: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used; test-code exemptions via cfg_attr; cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for error types; Option<T> for fallible operations; bounds checks on node.end_byte() <= source.len() before slicing; no unwrap in production code (test-only exemptions)

patterns: Language modules are standalone .rs files in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/ with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants
ELEMENT_QUERY captures function/method/class/interface/trait/enum declarations with @function and @class tags
DEFUSE_QUERY captures local variable declarations, assignments, and identifier reads with @write.* and @read.* tags
extract_inheritance walks tree-sitter AST from class node to find extends/implements clauses, returns Vec<String> of inheritance relationships
LanguageInfo struct registered in get_language_info() match statement with all query constants and handler function pointers
Tree-sitter language binding imported via workspace dependency (e.g., tree_sitter_java::LANGUAGE) and registered in get_ts_language() match
File extension mapped in lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP const array with (extension, language_name) tuples
Module registered via pub mod <lang> in mod.rs and referenced in get_language_info and get_ts_language
Tests use parse_<lang>(src) helper to create tree-sitter::Tree, then QueryCursor to validate queries and extract captures
constraints: All languages compiled unconditionally (no lang-* feature gates as of recent refactor)
tree-sitter-php grammar has two variants: php (with HTML) and php_only (PHP only); must choose one
PHP class_declaration has no parent_class/base_classes/interfaces fields; inheritance info lives in base_clause and class_interface_clause child nodes (not fields)
PHP method_declaration is the node kind for methods; function_definition is for top-level functions
DEFUSE_QUERY is optional but recommended for semantic analysis; Java and Python both define it
extract_inheritance, extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver are all optional handlers but recommended for languages with classes/methods
test_coverage: Existing language modules have inline unit tests covering: element query happy path (functions, classes, interfaces), call query, import query, inheritance extraction (single superclass, multiple interfaces, mixed), function name extraction, receiver type finding, and defuse query write/read sites. Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs exercise analyze_directory and analyze_file with real source files.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; grammar defines function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration nodes; class/interface/trait/enum have name field and body field; inheritance via base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) child nodes
library_findings.notes: Grammar has two variants (php with HTML, php_only without); node-types.json and grammar.js confirm field names and structure; base_clause and class_interface_clause are not fields but child nodes in the sequence

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter::Language, tree_sitter::Query, tree_sitter::QueryCursor, tree_sitter::Node with child_by_field_name(), named_child(), parent(), kind(), start_byte(), end_byte() methods
library_findings.notes: Standard tree-sitter Rust API; all language modules use identical patterns for query execution and node traversal

approaches.name: Minimal PHP support (CSS-like pattern)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY only; no DEFUSE_QUERY, no inheritance handlers. Register tree-sitter-php dependency in Cargo.toml and workspace, add mod php and match arms in mod.rs and lang.rs, add .php extension to EXTENSION_MAP. Mirrors CSS integration which has no defuse_query and no handlers.
pros: Smallest change surface; fastest to implement
Sufficient for basic symbol extraction (functions, classes, methods)
cons: No inheritance extraction; cannot answer 'what does this class extend'
Incomplete compared to Java/Python/Kotlin which all have DEFUSE_QUERY

approaches.name: Full PHP support with inheritance and defuse (recommended)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY constants; implement extract_inheritance, extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver handlers. Register in Cargo.toml, mod.rs, lang.rs. Add comprehensive unit tests covering functions, methods, classes, interfaces, traits, enums, inheritance patterns, and defuse sites.
pros: Full semantic analysis capability matching Java/Python/Kotlin
Supports def-use analysis for variable tracking
cons: Larger implementation; more code to test and maintain
Requires careful handling of PHP's base_clause and class_interface_clause node structure
More complex inheritance walk due to non-field child nodes

approaches.name: PHP with optional handlers (staged approach)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with all queries (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY) but only implement extract_inheritance handler initially; defer extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver to a follow-up PR. Register in Cargo.toml, mod.rs, lang.rs with None for unimplemented handlers.
pros: Inheritance support available from day one
Handlers can be added incrementally without breaking existing code
cons: Incomplete on day one; some queries may not be fully utilized

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP support with inheritance and defuse). The codebase has established patterns for complete language integration (Java, Python, Kotlin all have DEFUSE_QUERY and all handlers). PHP is a widely-used language and deserves parity with existing implementations. The effort is moderate and the result is production-ready. The inheritance walk, while non-trivial due to base_clause/class_interface_clause being child nodes rather than fields, is well-documented in the tree-sitter-php grammar and straightforward to implement.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
"
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-php grammar (common/define-grammar.js and php/src/node-types.json): class_declaration has a name field and a body field, but inheritance is encoded as child nodes (not fields) in the sequence: optional base_clause (which contains 'extends' keyword followed by names) and optional class_interface_clause (which contains 'implements' keyword followed by names). To extract inheritance, walk the class_declaration node's children: find base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes (not via child_by_field_name but via child_count/named_child iteration), then extract name nodes from within each. Each name node's text represents one base class (from base_clause) or one implemented interface (from class_interface_clause).
